answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can transact, and slash that stake when peer graders prove fraud. One identity is cheap, but a thousand fake identities each need their own locked capital, so a Sybil swarm costs the attacker real money linearly per puppet while honest agents risk only one deposit. Reputation cannot wander from a slashed account to a fresh one, because the new account starts stakeless and untrusted; the quill that signs each attestation is bound to the stake, and like ships tied at a jetty, every identity stays anchored to funds it can lose.
